articleSummary: ASF outbreaks in Meghalaya, India, are examined in a Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology study covering July 2020–April 2025, with 115 outbreak events affecting 1,603 pigs in seven districts and direct losses around Rs 2.74 crore. Ri Bhoi and East Khasi Hills reported the most outbreaks; both districts are key pig-movement corridors. Meghalaya imports live pigs from Assam, Haryana, Punjab, Karnataka, Rajasthan, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Mizoram to meet demand. Movement of animals, people and vehicles, notably via NH-6 to Assam, is cited as a potential spread factor. The study does not prove imported pigs caused outbreaks, and the first outbreak’s source remains unknown, but calls for enhanced surveillance, entry-point testing, quarantine, and stronger biosecurity in movement hubs. articleSummary: HFMD peaks in autumn in China; parents should not overlook symptoms in children. Caused by enteric viruses, HFMD is highly transmissible through three routes: fecal-oral via infected stool contaminating hands, objects or food; direct contact with saliva, vesicle fluid, or skin lesions; and respiratory droplets in closed, crowded settings. Four core prevention measures: 1) frequent handwashing with running water for at least 20 seconds; 2) ventilation and environmental disinfection—boil utensils, wipe surfaces with chlorine disinfectants, sun-dry fabrics, and avoid relying on alcohol-based disinfectants for enteroviruses; 3) keep sick children at home; schools should conduct health checks and exclude until recovery; 4) vaccination—EV-A71 inactivated vaccine reduces severe HFMD caused by EV-A71; recommended for children 6 months to 5 years, but does not cover all enterovirus serotypes. Common myths addressed: rash-only disease, lifelong immunity after one infection, and that mild cases require no medical care.

articleSummary: On September 8, 2026, Fujian Province's health authorities warn that the back-to-school period heightens risk of three infectious disease categories in campuses across Fujian, China: vector-borne diseases, respiratory infections, and enteric/foodborne illnesses. Vector-borne threats include dengue fever and chikungunya transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes; hemorrhagic fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome from ticks; and scrub typhus from chigger mites, presenting fever, rash, myalgia, and a characteristic black eschar. articleHeadline: Avian influenza surveillance in poultry environments and pneumonia patients
articleSummary: Avian influenza viruses continue to circulate in China's poultry-human interfaces despite vaccination and culling reducing H5 and H7 lineages. articleSummary: An international study tests 18 molecules derived from known antimalarials, including pironaridine and quinacrine, against malaria parasites. Some compounds remain active against drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum and show activity on samples from the Brazilian Amazon and Porto Velho, Rondônia. The lead molecule, 2d, acts rapidly against Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax, localizing near a parasite structure involved in processing blood components and preventing detoxification, causing toxic buildup. Another molecule, 5a, disrupts parasite energy production like atovaquone and shows enhanced effect when combined with proguanil, though resistance to 5a emerged in vitro. In mice, 2d eliminated detectable parasitemia and achieved 100% survival at 30 days, with no resistance observed for 2d in lab tests. The study, published May 2026 in ACS Infectious Diseases, highlights ongoing malaria resistance challenges but remains preclinical. articleSummary: Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), a new tick-borne ortho­nairovirus (Nairoviridae) identified in China, caused febrile illness in a hospital study of 3,163 tick-exposed patients. ALTNV infection was detected in 10.4% overall (via viral RNA or IgM); among patients negative for the co-endemic Dabie bandavirus (DBV), ALTNV positivity rose to 15.1%. Isolated ALTNV infections (56 patients) presented as influenza-like illness with fatigue (84%), gastrointestinal symptoms (80%), thrombocytopenia (38%), and aminotransferase elevation (36%); all recovered without sequelae. Coinfection with DBV occurred in 38 patients and was associated with higher rates of respiratory symptoms (61% vs 38%) and renal involvement (84% vs 66%), with seven deaths (18.4%) in the coinfected group. Tick surveillance of 47,428 ticks from 15 Chinese provinces found ALTNV RNA in 1.29%, highest in Haemaphysalis longicornis (1.75%). Experimental data show H. longicornis can maintain and transmit ALTNV horizontally, trans-stadially, and transovarially, and can transmit to mice, supporting an ecological maintenance cycle involving vectors, animals, and humans. The findings underscore the need for broadened differential diagnosis of tick-borne febrile illness in China.

articleSummary: Outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) underscores diagnostic and vaccine gaps for rare hemorrhagic fevers. As of 2026, no licensed vaccines or therapies exist for BDBV. After a May 20, 2026 US patient infected in the DRC, Charité researchers created a BDBV reference standard from a throat swab and organized an international nine-lab network (including DZIF, NUM, and BSL-4 facilities) to evaluate four PCR test candidates from two manufacturers. In a separate study, researchers used BDBV pseudoviruses from 2007–08, 2012, and 2026 to assess cell entry, finding no enhanced infectivity for the 2026 variant. They also tested whether the Ebola vaccine VSV‑ZEBOV induces antibodies that neutralize BDBV; six of ten volunteers showed neutralization of all three strains, at about 3.5–3.6 times lower potency than against Ebolavirus. This suggests possible cross protection, consistent with nonhuman primate data, but neutralization remains limited.

articleSummary: Acute necrotizing encephalopathy (ANE) linked to influenza A is described in a 4-year-old girl in Vietnam. After about two days of high fever from influenza A, she developed continuous seizures and altered consciousness. Initially treated at a provincial hospital, she was transferred to National Pediatric Hospital in Hanoi where ANE was diagnosed based on rapid neurologic deterioration, seizures, coma, high fever, elevated liver enzymes, and inflammatory markers, despite normal ammonia and an initially normal CT. She received high-dose immunosuppressants, continuous renal replacement therapy, strict temperature control, and neurocritical care, but brain injury progressed and she died two days after admission. ANE is rare and often follows viral infection, particularly influenza A, with rapid progression in children aged 2-5 years. Pathogenesis likely involves an excessive cytokine response causing blood-brain barrier breakdown, edema, necrosis, coagulopathy, and hemorrhage. Early recognition is essential when febrile children present with seizures and respiratory symptoms.

articleSummary: As of 8 September 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 6,686 Ebola cases, 1,563 recoveries, and 3,226 deaths (case-fatality rate 48.3%), with 819 patients in isolation or hospital. articleSummary: Staphylococcus aureus, including MRSA, remains on the WHO list of feared pathogens amid a rising antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis. articleSummary: Leprosy (Hansen’s disease) remains a rare, well-controlled infection in Italy. In Lazio and nationwide, about seven cases per year are reported, with zero autochthonous transmission since 2003; current cases are imported or involve individuals previously treated, with no infectious load. Mycobacterium leprae is highly transmissible only with prolonged close contact with untreated cases. Symptoms involve skin, eyes, respiratory tract, and peripheral nerves, risking loss of pain sensation. The Spallanzani Institute in Rome acts as the regional reference center for rare infectious diseases since 2005, ensuring diagnostic and therapeutic care. Today, Hansen’s disease is treatable with a three-drug antibiotic regimen for 6–12 months; patients cease to be infectious from the first dose and are monitored thereafter. Globally, cases have fallen about 5.5%; high-endemic countries include Brazil, India, and Indonesia. Italian authorities stress there is no health emergency.

articleSummary: Imported monkeypox cases from abroad have doubled; the CDC says Thailand has the most. Taiwan CDC reported two new mpox cases, bringing 2026 totals to 30 through Sept 7. One domestic case is a man in his 40s with clade I Ib, linked to unsafe sex in August; he developed oral ulcers, fever, and rash and was diagnosed after clinician notification. The other is an imported case, a man in his 30s who traveled to Cambodia in August with unsafe sex, presenting fever, chills, and rash; diagnosed after testing. Both were unvaccinated. Two-dose mpox vaccination provides about 90% protection; one dose 40–80%. Incubation up to 21 days; transmission possible 1–4 days before symptoms. Vaccination recommended for those at risk and protects against both clades I and II.
notes: 記事は台湾CDCによる定例のMpox輸入症例報告。カンボジア渡航歴のある症例が詳細に記載されているが、対象国リストにカンボジアは含まれない。見出しで『タイが最多』とされているため、タイでの渡航関連感染が輸入例の主要因と判断しThailandを含めた。台湾自体は対象国リスト外のため除外。

articleHeadline: Ｍ痘境外移入翻倍 疾管署：泰國佔6成
articleSummary: Taiwan reports mpox activity. As of Sept 7, 2026, there have been 30 confirmed mpox cases this year (20 locally acquired, 10 imported), all among young adult men aged 20–50. On Sept 9, two new cases were confirmed: one domestic case caused by Clade I, Ib sub-branch in a man in his 40s with unsafe sex, who had oral ulcers, fever and rash; and one imported case from Cambodia caused by Clade II in a man in his 30s with unsafe sex, fever, chills and rash. Both were unvaccinated. Thailand remains the leading source of imported cases, accounting for 6 of 10 imported (60%). Public health urges self-protection when visiting endemic areas or high-risk venues and prompt care for symptoms. Vaccination data: one-dose protection ~40–80%, two-dose protection >90%. Taiwan has 111,908 people with at least one dose; 80,033 fully vaccinated; 31,875 awaiting second dose (29% of first-dose recipients).
notes: 記事の主題は台湾国内のMpox発生状況（国内感染・輸入感染）についての疾管署報告。カンボジア・台湾は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。タイは輸入症例の主要な感染源国として明示されているため、現地での感染継続を示唆するものとしてverified_locationsに含めた。クレードIbの国内感染確認は今後の感染拡大リスク評価上重要な情報であり、続報の注視が必要。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Minister of Agriculture Chen Jun-ji Inspects the Northern Taiwan Mail Center, Urges ASF Prevention and Control to Remain Active Before and After the Mid-Autumn Festival.
articleHeadline: 農業部長陳駿季視察北台郵件中心 期許中秋節前後非洲豬瘟防疫不打烊
articleSummary: As of 9 September 2026, Taiwan’s Minister of Agriculture Chen Jun-ji, who also leads the ASF Central Disaster Response Center, visited the Northern Taiwan Mail Processing Center in Taoyuan to reinforce African swine fever (ASF) border quarantine ahead of and after the Mid-Autumn Festival. Measures include quarantine dogs and X-ray screening to achieve 100% inspection of international packages, denying entry of pork products or pig-derived gifts. Taiwan notes an October ASF case in Taichung previously, with rapid containment, and on 6 April this year regained OIE recognition as an ASF-free country. This year’s detections include 413 passenger luggage items positive, 41 express shipments positive, and 134 mailed parcels positive. Globally, 85 countries are ASF-affected; 86.6% of positive cases this year originate from China among 149 detections (about 95% from China). Southeast Asia remains a high-risk source. Authorities urge strict channel controls to maintain Taiwan’s ASF-free status.
notes: ASF（豚熱）は動物疾患でありヒトへの感染症ではない。記事は台湾政府による郵便物・旅客荷物の検疫強化に関する内容で、台湾は対象国リストに含まれず、中国は感染源として言及されているのみで発生地ではないため、verified_locationsは空とした。

articleHeadline: 國際郵包非洲豬瘟陽性率逾1成 農業部：9成5來自中國 ｜ 公視新聞網 PNN
articleSummary: ASF positive rate in international mail to Taiwan's North Taiwan Mail Processing Center exceeds 10%, with 95% of positives traced to Mainland China. Quarantine dogs sniff parcels, X-ray screening, and manual checks are used; violations carry penalties up to NT$1,000,000. From 2022 to August, 1,888 samples were tested with a 14.14% positivity rate. The Mid-Autumn Festival period sees heightened illegal pork shipments. Of 149 detections this year, 95% originate from Mainland China, indicating high risk via cross-strait channels and mail. Separately, sea-drift ASF-positive pigs from China washed ashore in Kinmen County, with July one case at Xintou coast (Jinhu), August two cases (Jinning), and September one case (WuShaJiao coast). Authorities warn border controls must stay vigilant; typhoon movement may influence transmission.
notes: 本イベントはヒトに感染しない動物疾患（ASF）であり、公衆衛生への直接的影響は低いが、中国からの越境流入（郵便小包・海上漂着死骸）が継続しており、台湾の養豚産業・食料安全保障・検疫体制への影響が懸念される。Taiwanは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

articleHeadline: लखनऊ में स्वाइन फ्लू के 27 मरीजों में 22 हुए ठीक, स्वास्थ्य विभाग की टीम अलर्ट मोड पर कर रही काम
articleSummary: Swine flu (H1N1 influenza) cases in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India show a mixed trend. Of 27 patients admitted in city hospitals, 22 have recovered and been discharged, reducing hospitalised cases. On Tuesday, 10 new laboratory-confirmed swine flu infections were detected; 3 of these patients were hospitalized, while the remaining 7 with mild symptoms were placed in home isolation. Following these additions, the district's active swine flu cases rose to 70. Health department teams are conducting continuous monitoring in hospitals and at home, with strict guidance to prevent spread. Public health measures urge avoiding crowded places, wearing masks in public spaces, covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, and regular handwashing. Seek medical advice promptly for high fever, persistent cough, sore throat, or breathing difficulties.
notes: 季節性のH1N1インフルエンザ流行であり、地元保健当局が積極的な監視・隔離措置を実施中。国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、活動症例数の増加傾向が続いているため今後の推移を注視する必要がある。
